featured_videos.title: Are BUGS A Carnivore Food?
featured_videos.creator: Dr. Tony Hampton - The Metabolic Health Doc
featured_videos.commentary: Here's what I'm noticing in these comments: people are drawing a pretty hard line between "interesting in theory" and "actually going to do it." And honestly, that tracks with what I see in the community. When bug protein gets pitched as the future of food or as some kind of sustainability play, our readers aren't interested. They've got ruminant meat. They know what works. The comment about "you will own nothing and be happy" tells you exactly where the pushback is coming from, too. But then you've got the people who actually eat bugs as a cultural thing (Southeast Asia) or as part of raising their own food (chickens eating grasshoppers, then eating the eggs), and that's a totally different conversation. It's not about replacing meat. It's about context. Dr. Hampton's approach of just trying it and reporting back feels honest, which is probably why people respect it even when they're not rushing out to eat grasshoppers themselves.

featured_videos.title: High Protein French Silk Pie With a Carnivore Crust
featured_videos.creator: Maria Emmerich
featured_videos.editorial_title: High Protein French Silk Pie With a Carnivore Crust
featured_videos.commentary: This is the kind of recipe that makes people realize carnivore desserts aren't just "acceptable" or "close enough" . they're actually *good*. The fact that Kai gave it his highest rating says something. What's interesting here is that Maria nailed the crust problem, which trips up a lot of people trying to bake low-carb. You can't just swap flour and expect the texture to work the same way. The comments about serving size and broken links are real though. when you find a recipe that actually lands, you want the details to match what you're making. If you're trying this, scale it up confidently for a crowd; the math works, and unlike grain-based desserts, it won't dry out sitting around.

featured_videos.title: This 2-Ingredient Carnivore Snack Is Way Too Good
featured_videos.creator: Meet Carnivore
featured_videos.editorial_title: This 2-Ingredient Carnivore Snack Is Way Too Good
featured_videos.commentary: The community's already running with this. Brown butter cream cheese bites sound simple until you read the comments and realize people are treating it like a gateway recipe, mixing in bacon, pork rinds, parmesan, even swirling it into carnivore ice cream. That's the vibe with the best carnivore snacks, honestly, they work because they're a blank canvas. Someone mentioned whipping the cream cheese while drizzling the butter in, and that's the kind of practical hack that gets saved and tried at 10 PM when a craving hits. The fact that people are shocked it tastes sweet without any sweetener at all is kind of the whole story of why browning butter matters, and why this format works where so many other "easy snack" ideas just sit unwatched.

featured_videos.title: 3 Years on the Carnivore Diet… Here's What Really Happened
featured_videos.creator: MISSMEAT Carnivore
featured_videos.editorial_title: 3 Years on the Carnivore Diet… Here's What Really Happened
featured_videos.commentary: What hits me most about this video is how honest she is about the non-linear part. Three years in and she's still adjusting, still figuring out what works, still occasionally stepping back. That's the real story nobody leads with. The comments mention healing as an up-and-down process, and that's exactly right. it's not "day one you're broken, day thirty you're fixed." One commenter went from an A1C of 14 to 6, which is massive, but even that took time and usually some tweaking along the way. For anyone starting out thinking they need to be perfect or they're doing it wrong, this is the antidote. The version of this way of eating you can actually stick with beats the pristine version you quit in three weeks, and her willingness to say that out loud matters.

featured_videos.title: Forget the Slow Cooker! My Favorite Oven Chuck Roast
featured_videos.creator: Ketogenic Woman
featured_videos.editorial_title: Forget the Slow Cooker! My Favorite Oven Chuck Roast
featured_videos.commentary: Chuck roast in the oven hits different than the slow cooker, and the comments here prove it. People are talking about the Maillard reaction, the umami, that old-school Sunday dinner flavor that actually matters when you're eating the same protein week after week. The sear-then-braise method works because you're building flavor first, not just cooking meat until it falls apart. That's the protocol that sticks around, not the one that's fastest. If you're meal prepping chuck like I do every Saturday, the oven method gives you something you'll actually want to eat on Tuesday instead of just tolerate.

featured_videos.title: The Lion Diet Did THIS to My Menopause
featured_videos.creator: HomeSteadHow
featured_videos.editorial_title: The Lion Diet Did THIS to My Menopause
featured_videos.commentary: The comments under this one tell the real story: women in their 50s getting regular periods back, periods that don't hurt, periods they thought were gone for good. That's not dramatic before-and-after content, that's someone's life changing quietly in ways that matter. What strikes me is how many people say the same thing happened to them, like Jen's experience just gave them permission to talk about their own. If you're watching this in perimenopause wondering if carnivore is worth it, the answer isn't about weight or energy or any of the usual stuff. it's about your cycle stabilizing when you thought that ship had sailed. That's the kind of result that makes people stick with this long-term, because you can't unsee it once your body starts working the way it's supposed to.
